input.cause: The "cut at the output limit" form is a mislabel. At step 8 of exp-control/t-2026-09-29-0001 (procedure.submit), the outcome is "cut", but the reason the harness recorded is "Provider proposed a capability outside the allowlist". No token limit is named. The same reason appears on every attempt linked to the form. So the harness labels an allowlist refusal of the provider's proposed call as a TRUNCATED (output limit) cut. The model proposed a capability that was not on the allowlist, and the harness reported that as a cut. The lead reads the drop from 5/6 to 0/10 as an improvement caused by the changed prompt and files. The sources show only that the labelled form disappeared. They do not show that output truncation was ever the failure. They do not show which change removed the off-allowlist proposals either. The fingerprint changes include the procedure prompt and 17 code files. The text length of specs/procedure/prompt.md is 3501 characters both at the task's version and today. So the prompt edit cannot be isolated as the cause.

predictions.alternative: the model really hit a small output-token limit (maxTokens) that the prompt change relieved

input.cause: The cuts were real. In the tasks before the change, procedure.submit at step 8 ended with completion = 4096 tokens, the Anthropic wire's default output cap, because the profile sets no maxTokens. The whole procedure and its long justifications list did not fit in that cap. The cap was the same before and after (4096), so the change did not raise it. After the change, 0 of 10 tasks hit the cap. I cannot attribute the relief to the prompt text alone: the procedure prompt has the same length at both versions (3501 chars), and 26 files changed together (memory, reflection, grammars, code). The model's output got shorter or took another path, not a bigger budget. The harness also labelled each cut "Provider proposed a capability outside the allowlist", which is a false reason for a truncated call. The lead is right that the form went away with the change. It is wrong to read it as one prompt edit.

input.summary: Diagnosis diag-193d614066bf was accepted by the guard (sha256 8ece6ea0e4b4…). The sources it rests on show that the truncations were cuts at the 4096-token output limit. Before the change, claude-sonnet-5-5 had a procedure.submit step cut in 5 of 6 tasks. Example: step 8 of task exp-control/t-2026-09-29-0001, which produced a 4096-token completion. profiles/anthropic.json sets no maxTokens, so the Anthropic wire's default of 4096 applied both before and after the change. After the change (fingerprint b955c2ab8a73, and 7890280cb9b1 for the later runs), 0 of 10 tasks were cut, and the rate is 0 of 5 under fingerprint 7890280cb9b1. I did not find which of the changed slots made the difference. The changed slots are the procedure prompt, the reflection/memory files, the scenario and the code. The cause is therefore the output-limit default combined with long procedure submissions, and the later changes reduced it. Whether it still holds today is only partly settled. Today's profile for profiles/anthropic.json (a haiku model) still sets no explicit maxTokens, so the limit itself has not changed. The cause is therefore not closed at the profile, and a long submission could be cut again.
